question.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{y}^{2}}{x}$ is enclosed between the curve  $x=2-{y}^{2}$ and the line $x=1$ for $-1\le y\le 1.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type II plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14194035/assets/6c78767d03e3429551498e651d982d99b6ceb72aa73422c5205bef296c9a1754.png)

So, we have 

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2-{y}^{2},\,-1\le y\le 1\}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{y}^{2}}{x}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot \frac{15{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}15{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2-{y}^{2}}15{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{y}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{2-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{y}^{2}[x]_{x=1}^{x=2-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{y}^{2}(2-{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{y}^{2}-15{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[5{y}^{3}-3{y}^{5}]}_{y=-1}^{y=1} \\  & =(5-3)-(-5+3) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
